answer: Persistent work anchor. Each identity must accumulate a public history of completed tasks before it can bid; the record is bound to a hardware key and an opal-signed attestation that cannot be transferred. Cloning resets the history to zero, so a fresh clone earns nothing until it redoes the full ramp. An ember fee is charged per attestation and rises with each new key seen from the same sponsor, making each marginal clone cost more than its expected early earnings.
